description: An account of how humans have manufactured the color blue: ancient Egyptian kilns, lazurite extracted from Afghan lapis lazuli for expensive European painting, Prussian blue in Berlin and Hokusai’s woodblock prints, synthetic ultramarine, indigo dye and colonial labor, and the gallium-nitride work that made efficient blue LEDs possible. The essay explains the difference between seeing the blue sky, reflecting blue light from a pigment, dyeing cloth, and generating blue light electrically, without turning the history into a simple story of ever-improving progress.
